feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications role: it presents clear progression, relevant scope, and a solid mix of strategy, technical, and operational leadership. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, fewer repeated themes, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility and leadership across digital strategy, content, analytics, and multimedia.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms and scale indicators: Drupal migration, 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, analytics stack, and studio buildout.  
- Writing is professional and readable, with consistent tone and strong alignment to mission-driven/public-sector communications work.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics where possible: traffic growth, email performance, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, cost savings, or team size managed.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize punctuation in lists (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, systems”); and consider replacing “French (A2/Learning)” with “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or serious grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Add one or two concrete signals of seniority or domain focus, such as public-sector, advocacy, or mission-driven organizations.
- Tighten the list of channels to avoid sounding broad but vague; emphasize strategy, operations, and platform leadership.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal and platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” and “advocacy messaging” also recur in experience entries, so keep the intro concise.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive, high-value capabilities rather than broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more specific, senior-level wording: “Digital transformation strategy,” “CMS governance & administration,” “Editorial operations & workflow design,” “Analytics, dashboards & performance reporting.”
- Replace vague or awkward phrasing: change “Multi-channel communication” to “Multi-channel communications leadership” and “Workflow & systems architecture” to “Content operations & systems design.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve scanability; suggested version:
  Digital transformation strategy • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS governance & web administration • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, dashboards & performance reporting • Content operations & systems design • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several points already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy messaging, and stakeholder coordination.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale.

Suggested edit
- Open with the client and mandate: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Led enterprise web and content-operations improvements across Drupal, analytics, and cross-channel communications workflows.
- Built modular campaign microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits within Drupal for repeatable campaign delivery.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties, improving publishing efficiency and site usability.
- Shaped an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery experience.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, turnaround time, campaign launches, search accuracy, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo and the summary; keep only if tied to a distinct result.
- AI search and microsites already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national association serving county officials.”
- Combine and streamline web modernization: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements in publishing speed, reporting adoption, engagement, production cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance from the in-house studio.
- Tighten remaining bullets to action + result: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, expanding advocacy and event production capacity” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on leadership, modernization, and systems.
- Video-program growth also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize the studio build and organizational capacity shift here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid mid-level progression item, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Emphasize executional leadership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth outcomes rather than broad ownership language.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy content across teams.”
- Replace “helping” phrasing with direct action: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams around more consistent content production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director role’s opening line.
- Weekly video/livestream language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling and coordination, not firsts unless clearly distinct.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme alignment with the CV, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. Tightening it around senior-level differentiators will make it more credible and less repetitive.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused content planning” beside “leadership.”
- If space allows, emphasize systems/scale over general content language, since that is the stronger recent-career signal.
- Consider dropping “messaging” for “communications” or “stakeholder communications” to sound more executive and less campaign-copy focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and implementation themes tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they are most supported by recent roles and projects.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority platform if space is tight; “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” can be grouped as “additional CMS platforms.”
- If possible, align wording with impact shown elsewhere: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this section strategic and save full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; keep only if it remains a clear differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making impact, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Tighten and group related tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language like “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid listing every analytics tool here if they already appear in Technical + IT; Topline Skills should signal senior-level capability.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies (“multimedia production and livestream operations”) and Technical + IT (“Livestream studio workflows,” podcast production). Tighten it to emphasize higher-level delivery capability and recent studio/event leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia, Studio & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, less tool-like bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery
- Studio buildout and operations management
- Multi-camera/PTZ production workflows
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale language such as “recurring advocacy programming” or “in-house studio production” to connect to recent NACo impact.
- Keep phrasing outcome-oriented; “PTZ camera systems” alone reads too equipment-specific for a topline skills section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially repeat Core Competencies.
- Tool-specific items here also overlap with Technical + IT; keep this section strategic, not inventory-like.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating names only.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/scope: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and consider trimming lower-value items if space is tight: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages
- If accurate, add version or context for credibility: “Drupal 10” or “SharePoint Online”
- Keep GitHub Pages only if it supports a meaningful project; otherwise replace with a more relevant platform or capability

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [2]; differentiate by adding platform context/specialization here rather than repeating the same list
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear elsewhere, so don’t add them here unless tied to a specific platform

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, analytics, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML/CSS/JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; it adds little value.
- If accurate, replace one generic item with a higher-impact recent capability, e.g. **search/retrieval implementation**, **CMS theming**, or **deployment automation** to better reflect current consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears under Topline Skills; keep the fuller phrasing in one place only.
- **API integrations** and workflow-related tooling also overlap with Core Competencies and Automation/Workflow Systems.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Tighten and group by function: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: **Built and managed workflow systems using Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier; coordinated delivery through Jira, Asana, Trello, and Basecamp; supported team operations in Slack and Microsoft Teams.**
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools; consider dropping 1–2 lower-signal items if not used recently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; grouping them separately avoids muddy positioning.
- Repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, so this item should stay concise and tool-focused.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and under-leverages your recent leadership in email operations. It should signal scale or use case, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms** for clearer relevance.
- Reorder by strongest/recentest fit: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp** if Higher Logic was primary at NACo.
- Add brief functional qualifiers if space allows: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Platforms supporting newsletters and engagement programs reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets already showing email leadership; avoid repeating audience scale here if you add it elsewhere in a summary/skills section.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t imply CRM/marketing automation depth beyond what you directly used.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs rather than generic channel support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and founding-team impact: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital media team…”
- Tighten scope and use stronger verbs: “improved workflows across web, email, social and video” instead of “strengthening workflows.”
- Add measurable outputs if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or team size.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital media team, improving workflows across web, email, social and video. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this entry as launching/producing the series rather than expanding it.
- “Website refresh” may blur with the 2022–2024 redesign; keep this framed as an earlier refresh, not enterprise modernization.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope + standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support policy communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add a measurable result: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder reach, or types of programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid broad claims about leading digital strategy here, since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.
